name: Delayed Encephalopathy Due to Carbon Monoxide Poisoning

criteria.description: History of acute carbon monoxide poisoning with initial recovery
Latent asymptomatic period of 2 to 40 days following initial recovery
Development of neuropsychiatric symptoms including cognitive decline, motor deficits, or behavioral changes after latent period
MRI showing bilateral symmetric white matter lesions in cerebral hemispheres and basal ganglia
Exclusion of other causes of delayed encephalopathy such as infections or metabolic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prior carbon monoxide poisoning with initial recovery, followed by a latent period and subsequent development of neurological deterioration
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by neuroimaging and exclusion of other causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated brain choline level by MRS
Reduced brain N-acetyl aspartate level by MRS

laboratory: Elevated carboxyhemoglobin levels during acute phase
Normal routine blood tests during delayed phase
imaging: MRI showing bilateral symmetric white matter hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR

distinguishingFeatures: Immediate neurological symptoms without latent period
MRI lesions involving periventricular white matter with dissemination in time and space
History of hypoxic event other than CO poisoning
Different clinical context and imaging findings

redFlags: Rapid onset of neuropsychiatric symptoms after latent period
Progressive cognitive decline with motor deficits
MRI showing extensive bilateral white matter lesions
references: Choi IS. Delayed neurologic sequelae in carbon monoxide intoxication. Arch Neurol. 1983;40(7):433-435.
Weaver LK. Clinical practice. Carbon monoxide poisoning. N Engl J Med. 2009;360(12):1217-1225.
Rose JJ, Wang L, Xu Q, et al. Carbon monoxide poisoning: pathogenesis, management, and future directions of therapy. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2017;195(5):596-606.
